body: - Every time bound viola holds (wait timeout and cap, MCP call deadline, dialog hold, send readiness gate, confirmation windows, agents read, the start's Claude config lock wait) falls on the driver, viola's child or viola's own start; no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. An MCP frame tool call (send, wait, last, answer) that outlives the MCP call deadline (`viola_mcp::MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`) ends `instance-unreachable` / `call-deadline`, the outcome of a send unknown; only the MCP frame tools write that detail, never the CLI, whose exit-21 cause set stays six. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list` and `viola revive` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP`, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` at `WAIT_CAP`: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched.

- Success = `isError:false` + the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent`; refusal = `isError:true` + `{refusal, detail}` + text `refused: <reason>` (a peer's `refusal` that is no code word reads `unknown`, a string `detail` that is no code word `null`, and a non-string `detail` no known reply); unreachable / fault = `isError:true` + `{"error":"instance-unreachable"|"wrapper-fault","detail":…}` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail` its cause word, built by `result::unreachable(cause)` from a `viola_core::UnreachableCause`: `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused` · `call-deadline` (MCP's alone, `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`'s expiry), `of_reply` reading `Connect` as `InstanceDead` and `Closed | Io` as `EndpointLost`, `of_board` the board's refusal as `StrictModes`, and `tools.rs` `frame` no `live_endpoint` through `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`, a refused `viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir` after `live_endpoint` as `SocketDir` and a refused `peer_admitted(client.server_euid())` or a failed `server_verified` as `ServerVerify`, each with no frame and no line, `isError` the record; `wrapper-fault` with the JSON-RPC fault's `{code,message,data}` as `viola_channel::sanitised_fault` reads it: a fixed `message`, `data` a closed object or null); a frame tool (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`) first runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on the home and the target instance, before `live_endpoint` (a refusal returns the `instance-unreachable` result with `detail: "strict-modes-failed"`, text `refused: instance-unreachable`, and writes no frame and no line); a frame tool whose connected server is not the recorded wrapper (on Unix its peer euid not this user's or unreadable, `peer_admitted`; else its peer pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or the check cannot be made; either reads `UnreachableCause::ServerVerify`; the start time read on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`) returns the `instance-unreachable` result with `detail: "server-verify-failed"`, no frame written and no log line. Every `isError` text is `refused: <code>`, and every MCP error result carries codes and fixed messages only, no path and no upstream text, each body a row of `MCP_RESULTS` in `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`. JSON-RPC errors are the MCP connection's own faults, an unknown tool name (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault (any other channel error, a reply of no known shape, a `wait` / `last` refusal, a panicked call), which is `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`.

- MCP `wait` sends `timeout_ms` = `min(given, WAIT_CAP)` (`viola_mcp::WAIT_CAP`, `wait_timeout`), `WAIT_CAP` when none is given, and `after` as given: below the MCP call deadline (`MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`), itself below the client's tool-call bound, so a wait returns before either cuts the call. Every frame tool call (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`; `list` is not under it) is bounded by that compiled call deadline: at expiry the call's work is dropped and the tool returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `call-deadline`.

- Success: `isError:false` + the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent`; refusal, unreachable, fault or invalid params: `isError:true` + codes only, text `refused: <code>`; `instance-unreachable` carries its cause in `detail` through `result::unreachable(cause)`: `of_reply` reads `Connect` as `instance-dead` and `Closed | Io` as `endpoint-lost`, `of_board` the board's refusal as `strict-modes-failed`, and `tools.rs` `frame` a refused `check_instance` as `strict-modes-failed`, no `live_endpoint` by `without_endpoint`, a refused `check_endpoint_dir` after `live_endpoint` as `socket-dir-refused` and a refused `peer_admitted` or a failed `server_verified` as `server-verify-failed`, and a frame tool call reaching its call deadline as `call-deadline` (MCP's alone, never a CLI exit-21 cause), `isError` the only record; JSON-RPC errors are only the connection's own faults, an unknown tool (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault (`-32603` `internal error`, `data: null`); `tools/list` and `server/discover` each carry `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private` (claude 2.1.287 drops every tool without them). rmcp features exactly `server` + `transport-io`; `viola mcp`'s stdin reaches rmcp only through `viola_mcp::stdin::CappedLines` at `MAX_FRAME` per line (rmcp reads stdio lines unbounded), an over-long line refused whole, never truncated or skipped, and ending the session as a closed stdin does; every call returns below the client's tool-call timeout: each frame tool call (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`; `list` is not under it) is bounded by a compiled call deadline (`viola_mcp::MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`), at expiry its work dropped and `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `call-deadline` returned, and MCP `wait` sends `timeout_ms` = `min(given, WAIT_CAP)` (`viola_mcp::WAIT_CAP`), `WAIT_CAP` when none is given, below that deadline, itself below the client's tool-call bound; on the MCP surface the deadline bounds the driver's wait, never the send itself.

- Time only through the injected `viola_core::Clock` (no mock_instant; no paused Tokio clock; `viola-mcp`'s MCP call deadline (`MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`) comes through its injected deadline provider, which a test fires by a signal, never by waiting it out — its `wait` bound is the pure `wait_timeout(given)`, a unit case), or an instant handed to a pure time decision as an argument; a link line's `since`, which `LinkSet::line` stamps from the wall clock outside the seam, is asserted by its shape only (`is_clock_time` in `tests/cli_links.rs`); never use an in-process clock to control another process's time.

- **Path 3 — `wait` / `last`** — wakes only on driver-relevant kinds (activity and wheel records, and a harness-origin `prompt-submitted`, never wake a parked `wait`), returns already-logged events at once, typed timeout, exit 21 on a vanished wrapper (`detail` `endpoint-lost` for a wrapper killed under a parked `wait`, after `cleanup` `instance-dead` in a kept home or `unwrapped-name` in a removed one; MCP the same body less `v`, `mcp_tools_a_wrapper_killed_under_a_parked_wait_reads_endpoint_lost`; the MCP `send`, `wait`, `last` and `answer` alone end with `detail` `call-deadline` at the MCP call deadline (`MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`), the frame dropped, a body with no CLI document, and a reply arriving before the deadline is returned as the reply); as landed, the cli + wrapper-channel half (`tests/cli_wait_last.rs`, `tests/chaos_wait_vanish.rs`) in CI on `ubuntu-latest`, the MCP `wait` / `last` steps landed at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` `mcp_tools_path2_path3_send_wait_last_match_the_cli`, each result compared with the CLI's `--json` document less `v`); the end-to-end wake witness of all three dialog kinds landed with Path 4 (`question` / `plan` in `path4_dialogs_…`, `permission` in `path4_permission_…`, where a PostToolUse `activity` line wakes no `wait`); a Stop's `turn-ended` data carries `background_tasks`, the Stop array's length or `null`, and `scheduled_wakes`, the Stop payload's `session_crons` array length or `null` (the key absent, null or not an array, and on an API-error end; it reaches `events.ndjson`, CLI `wait --json` and MCP `wait` only, never `last`, `list`, the snapshot or the replay), and an API-error turn end's carries `cause` too, absent on a Stop and one of nine closed words (`rate-limited`, `overloaded`, `auth-failed`, `billing`, `invalid-request`, `model-not-found`, `server-error`, `output-limit`, `api-error`) (`tests/hook_events.rs` `hook_a_recorded_stop_carries_its_background_task_count` over the recorded 2.1.287 `Stop.default.json`, so 0, with `state_events_background_tasks_and_option_details_are_known_keys`; a non-zero and a `null` count unit-tier; live on 2.1.296 on the Linux dev host, a local measurement and no suite, a product `wait --json` woke on `turn-ended` with `background_tasks` 0 and `last` read the turn)

- `viola revive`'s start arm logs as process `run` once its instance check has passed (`run-<name>.ndjson`, each preflight refusal — `already-live` (a live holder or a fresh replayed beat), `stale-heartbeat` (a stale holder), `no-session`, `session-live`, `cwd-missing` — one `process-exit{exit_code:1, detail}`; its `session-live` reading, skipped under `--fork` and passing on a failed read, writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"agents-probe"}` pair there, plus one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}` on an oversize or malformed answer); `viola revive --list` is role `cli` (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract; the sixth exemption retired): after its strict-modes check passes and only under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` it writes `process-start` / `process-exit` (`exit_code` 0 with no detail; `exit_code` 1 `detail:"no-session"` on an empty chain) into the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`, with no name no log, and its dispatch `Err` or panic reaches the `cli` catch site. A refused instance check on either `viola revive` arm (start or `--list`), or `viola mcp`'s refused `viola_state::strict::check_path` of its home or `diagnostics/` (run before its `mcp` role file opens; exit 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr), or `viola plugin install`'s refused `check_path` of its home or a `marketplace/` tree dir (run before its `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the stderr pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), or `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused `check_instance` of the driven instance (run before their `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), opens no role file and writes no line (the seventh exemption). So does a refused strict-modes check on the hook event and dialog paths (exit 0, nothing printed), on `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` or `release` (exit 21, the instance pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), on `viola verify`'s home tree (exit 1, the home pair) or on the home tree of `viola run` or `viola revive`'s start arm (exit 1, the home or the instance pair) (the eighth exemption). A refused peer euid (Unix) or a failed server check (the peer pid and start-time comparison, run on Linux, the one target) sends no frame and opens no `channel.request`: the eight CLI frame verbs (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`; `link` / `unlink` into the driven instance's `cli-<driven>.ndjson`) end `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside their dispatch span with no `channel-request` line; `viola hook` writes `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN (on a dialog hook `hook-invoked{corr:null}` first, then `decision_emitted:false`); MCP's frame tools return `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and no line, as their refused `check_endpoint_dir` (made after `live_endpoint`) does with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` and no frame, and as the liveness pre-check's does with `without_endpoint`'s reading (`instance-dead` or `unwrapped-name`) and as their own refused `check_instance` of the home and the instance directory does (made before `live_endpoint`, `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, no frame), and as `send`, `wait`, `last` and `answer` do at the MCP call deadline, `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE` (`detail` `call-deadline`, a cause the MCP frame tools alone write and the CLI never does; the frame dropped); no pid, start time, path or endpoint in any line. A refused socket directory (`check_socket_dir`, the strict-modes read verdict) is none of these exemptions and writes under its own closed word `socket-dir-refused`, with no path, pid or uid in any line: `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start (`socket_dir_ready`, no span, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create, a lost race and a refused check read one code, and a `Server::bind` failure is not this refusal) one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, under `viola revive --json` the same-shaped `socket-dir-refused` document; the eight CLI frame verbs one `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"socket-dir-refused", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside their dispatch span, no `channel-request` line and no frame; `viola hook` one `hook-decision{detail:"socket-dir-refused"}` at WARN inside `hook.handle` (on a dialog hook after `hook-invoked{corr:null}`, with `decision_emitted:false`), exit 0, empty streams and no frame.

title: 2026-11-21 — A leaf names a time bound by its constant, never its figure

data.head: ## 2026-11-21 — A leaf names a time bound by its constant, never its figure

body:
A rule file or a docs leaf that states one of viola's compiled bounds names the constant (`WAIT_CAP`,
`MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`, `GATE_MAX_WAIT`), never its value: the code holds the figure, no master row restates it, and a
figure copied into a leaf goes stale silently the day the constant moves. A comparer's or curator's draft that
carries the number is corrected to the name before it lands. The same holds for a reading of the claude CLI's
own bounds (its MCP tool-call limits): a leaf says it is a per-version reading of the bundle's strings and gives
no number.

Every MCP frame tool call (send, wait, last, answer) now ends at a compiled 55 s MCP call deadline; at the deadline the call returns the instance-unreachable result with the new cause word call-deadline, and list stays outside the deadline.
The closed unreachable-cause set grew from six members to seven (call-deadline), written by the MCP frame tools alone; the CLI exit-21 cause set is unchanged at six.
The MCP wait cap stays 50 000 ms; its reason is re-based from the claude 2.1.287 reading to the 2.1.328 and 2.1.330 bundles' client bound (read as 120 s auto-background, never measured), so the order is wait cap below call deadline below client bound.
Measured live on a new test-only rig arm MB: on claude 2.1.330 and 2.1.328 a wait with no timeout_ms returned whole at the 50 s cap; under a 5000 ms per-server timeout the client cut the call at 5 s and viola mcp outlived the cut call.
Finding, not fixed: the deadline bounds only the driver's wait; the wrapper's paste into the PTY stays one blocking write with no time bound, and at the deadline the wrapper's send goes on with its outcome unknown, as with endpoint-lost.
The viola-mcp adapter now runs a Tokio timer for the production deadline, with the deadline injected as a seam in tests (no paused Tokio clock).
